transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello, Mr. Mbeki. Thank you for agreeing to sit down with me.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I already know something happened. The nurse mentioned it before she left the room.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know you've heard some of this already, and I can see you're feeling tense. It's a very difficult situation to be in.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm not tense, I'm just wondering why I'm still sitting here waiting for an explanation. My business doesn't run itself.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I completely understand that your time is valuable and that being away from your work is a huge stress. I want to be very clear about what happened.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Go ahead then.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was a mistake with how your imaging was handled. Some things didn't go quite right with the files.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What does that mean? What mistake?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We had an issue with the system where some information got mixed up. Because of that, the team didn't have the right picture for the surgical plan.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Which picture? My MRI? Was it the wrong one?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was some confusion with the accession numbers. It wasn't a smooth process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't understand. Are you saying you looked at someone else's scan?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The system had a glitch, and it meant the wrong study was associated with your chart.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So you've been planning my surgery based on another person's body?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am very sorry that this happened. Our team is responsible for this error, and we apologize for the failure in our process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can't believe this. I've missed three days of work already. Now what? Do I have to stay another week? Is the surgery cancelled?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can hear how frustrating this is, especially with the financial pressure of your business. I know that every hour you spend here is an hour you aren't earning.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Exactly. I can't just tell my clients I'm hanging out in a hospital because the doctors can't tell two people apart.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is completely unfair that this is adding to your burden. I'm sitting here with you and I recognize how upsetting this is.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But you still haven't told me exactly what happened. You keep saying "confusion" and "glitches."

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The process for storing the images wasn't followed correctly, and that led to the wrong scan being viewed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So whose scan did you look at? And did you actually use it to decide where to cut me?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We had a breakdown in the verification steps. I am sorry.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm sorry isn't going to pay my rent this month.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You're right. An apology doesn't fix the lost time or the money you're losing right now. I acknowledge that.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So what is the plan? Do I get a new scan?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are going to resolve this. First, I am going to personally verify your correct images with the radiology lead within the next hour.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And then?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Once I've confirmed we have the right images, the lead surgeon will come in to review them with you by 5:00 PM today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And the surgery date?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is the second step. We will determine if the original date still works or if we need to shift it. I will give you a definitive answer on the schedule by tomorrow morning.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And I just have to sit here and wait?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: While we do that, I want you to keep a list of any specific questions you have for the surgeon so we don't miss anything during that 5:00 PM meeting.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'll do that. But I want a guarantee this doesn't happen again.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear that. I'm going to file a formal incident report today to ensure the radiology department changes how they label these files. We will make sure your records are double-checked by two different people before any one more step is taken.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I hope so. I just want to get out of here.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know you do. I'm going to go speak with radiology now, and I will be back in your room before 2:00 PM to update you.

H.justification: The resident never interrupts, remains regulated despite the patient's frustration, and allows the patient to fully express their concerns.

E.justification: The resident relies on platitudes and hedging ('things didn't go quite right', 'confusion', 'glitches') and only admits the wrong scan was viewed after the patient repeatedly prompts for a clear explanation.

A.justification: The resident uses direct apology language, explicitly states 'Our team is responsible for this error', and maintains accountability when the patient mentions financial loss.

R.justification: The resident names specific emotions ('tense', 'frustrating', 'upsetting') and references the patient's specific stress regarding his business and income.

T.justification: The resident provides specific steps with timelines (radiology lead within an hour, surgeon by 5:00 PM, schedule by tomorrow), assigns the patient a role (keeping a list of questions), and addresses prevention (incident report and double-checking).
